medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily; increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks if tolerated, then titrate to 10 mg to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose change
medications.purpose: Hypertension control and renal‑protective effect in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends an ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive for patients with metabolic syndrome or early CKD

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile review at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in a patient with QRISK ≥10% (assumed high) and metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 advises a statin for adults with QRISK ≥10% or ≥2 metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal; increase to 500 mg twice daily after 1 week, then to 850 mg twice daily as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong — HbA1c review every 3 months, renal function review annually
medications.purpose: Management of pre‑diabetes and weight reduction in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes (HbA1c 6.0% and BMI ≥30 kg/m²)

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially after first ACE‑I dose
interactions_checked.action: Start ramipril at low dose; monitor BP and consider reducing amlodipine to 1.25 mg or stopping once target BP achieved

interactions_checked.interaction: ACE‑I can raise serum potassium, risk of hyperkalaemia
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and eGFR in 7‑10 days; if K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L, reduce dose or switch to ARB

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase plasma concentrations of some statins; atorvastatin is less affected but still requires caution
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin (not simvastatin); monitor for myopathy and CK if muscle symptoms develop

contraindications.reason: Risk of lactic acidosis in severe renal impairment (NICE NG28)
contraindications.alternative: Delay initiation until eGFR measured; if eGFR <30, consider DPP‑4 inhibitor or lifestyle alone

contraindications.reason: Can worsen hypertension, renal function and potassium retention in metabolic syndrome (NICE CG181)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for analgesia; avoid chronic NSAID use

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² for ACE‑I dosing and metformin initiation; will obtain renal function before finalising metformin
Lipid profile (total, LDL, HDL) missing – assumed dyslipidaemia based on metabolic syndrome; statin will be reviewed after labs
QRISK score not calculated – assumed ≥10% given age, BMI, hypertension and pre‑diabetes; will calculate once smoking status and full labs are available
Liver function tests not available – will order before starting atorvastatin
Allergy status unknown – will confirm no ACE‑I or statin allergy before prescribing
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 2.5 mg daily (titrate to 10 mg) for hypertension and renal protection, add atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for primary CVD prevention, and initiate metformin MR 500 mg daily (titrate to therapeutic dose) for pre‑diabetes, pending eGFR confirmation. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, renal function, liver enzymes, and HbA1c as per NICE guidelines. Adjust amlodipine dose if needed and provide lifestyle counselling (diet, exercise, weight‑loss programme).
